function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a given command using the os.system() function specifically for Windows operating systems. For multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For complex tasks, create and run a .bat file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The Windows command line instruction(s) to be executed. Use '&&' between commands for multiple instructions. For complex sequences, encapsulate the logic within a .bat file and provide the execution command here.

message.reasoning:
The user says "start Docker on window using docker start." They want to start Docker on Windows using docker start. But docker start is used to start containers, not the Docker service itself. To start Docker Desktop or Docker Engine on Windows, you typically use services or Docker Desktop UI. On Windows, you can start Docker via the Docker Desktop application or via PowerShell: Start-Service Docker. Or if using Docker Desktop, you might need to launch Docker Desktop app. The user likely wants to start Docker engine. So we should explain that docker start starts containers, not the Docker daemon. To start Docker service, use Start-Service Docker or open Docker Desktop. Provide commands.

We have a tool to execute commands. We could call Start-Service Docker. But we don't know if the user has admin rights. We can provide the command but not actually execute it? The tool will execute. We can call the function with command "Start-Service Docker". That will attempt to start the Docker service. Alternatively, we can instruct to run "net start com.docker.service" or "sc start DockerDesktopService". But the simplest: "Start-Service Docker".

Thus we can respond with explanation and then call the function.
